issues.problem: This is a placeholder (the Unix epoch), not the date the content was checked against the sources. The guide defines `meta.verified` as the date of the real check. The validator accepts it because it is not in the future, but it falsely marks the question as verified and would be stale in any freshness reporting. The link excerpts were fetched on 2026-11-13.
issues.suggestedFix: Set `verified: 2026-11-13` (or the actual date of the re-check, not later than today UTC).

issues.claim: "the layer is deleted together with the monolith"
issues.problem: The Strangler Fig and Anti-corruption Layer pages in the excerpts do not say the ACL always goes away with the legacy system. The ACL page only suggests retiring it if it is not a permanent part of the solution. Stated as a rule, this is slightly too strong.
issues.suggestedFix: Soften in both locales: "and the layer is typically retired together with the monolith, unless it stays as a permanent boundary" / "а сам слой обычно выводят из эксплуатации вместе с монолитом, если он не остаётся постоянной границей".

issues.claim: "Как менять систему по частям, если пользователи всё это время продолжают обращаться к ней по одному и тому же адресу?"
issues.problem: The hint points fairly directly at the facade/proxy, which is only step 3 of the reference answer. It does not give away the whole answer, so it is acceptable, but it is on the strong side. RU and EN agree in strength.
issues.suggestedFix: Optionally weaken it, e.g. "Что должно стоять между пользователями и системой, чтобы части можно было заменять по одной?" (EN: "What could sit between users and the system so that parts can be replaced one at a time?").
